data.description:
## Context

Found by the Step-7 parity sweep of bug `intangible-ladyish-vicuna` (`93a9-66cf-e681-4f49`),
which restored the compaction trigger's sidecars to the canonical store.

`doctor_locks.scan_locks` (`src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py:321-360`) canonicalises the
tracker and then reports four legs — `tickets-write-fcntl`, `tickets-write-mkdir`, `hlc`,
`enrich-drain` (`doctor_locks.py:90-93`). There is NO leg for `compact-worker.lock`, even
though it is a stamped advisory lock in the same `.rebar/`, arbitrated by the same
`lock_owner.stamped_file_is_stale` decision table as the drain lock next to it.

Consequence: a compaction worker that dies between acquire and release leaves a stamped lock
that `rebar doctor` cannot see, so the one diagnostic built to answer "who holds what" is
silent about the lock most likely to be held by a detached background process. (The lock IS
self-healing via the shared staleness table, so this is observability, not correctness.)

Note: the `intangible-ladyish-vicuna` description asserted that "`rebar doctor` describes the
canonical `compact-worker.lock`". It does not — that assumption was checked and disproved
during the debug session, which is what surfaced this gap.

## Scope

Add a `compact-worker` leg to `scan_locks` alongside `enrich-drain`, reusing the existing
stamped-file report helper. Deliberately NOT done inside the bug fix: adding a doctor leg is
new capability, and that fix was held to restoration only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar doctor` reports a `compact-worker` lock leg, on the canonical store, with the
      same held-for / staleness / holder detail the `enrich-drain` leg carries.
- [ ] A test covers a held compact-worker lock appearing in the census and a free store not
      reporting a spurious holder.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, complexity ratchet and the unit sweep green.
data.title: doctor's lock census has no compact-worker leg
